extracted.intended_audience: PolitiFact journalists, other fact-checkers, and readers seeking transparency about PolitiFact's methodology
extracted.subtask_description: PolitiFact's formal methodology for selecting claims, sourcing and reporting fact-checks, assigning Truth-O-Meter and Flip-O-Meter ratings, tracking campaign promises, and handling corrections. Focused on independent fact-checking of political/public claims and promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-checking journalism is the heart of PolitiFact. Our core principles are independence, transparency, fairness, thorough reporting and clear writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles are the raison d'être for publishing: to give citizens information they need to govern themselves. They inform all selection, reporting, rating and correction decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence and ownership rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on coverage, what facts to check, and Truth-O-Meter ratings are determined solely by PolitiFact’s independent journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PolitiFact is owned by the nonprofit Poynter Institute; contracts and grant agreements include clauses asserting editorial independence so donors, advertisers or grantmakers do not influence content or ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding transparency and donor restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact discloses any individual donation or grant in excess of $1,000 and organizations that contributed more than 5 percent of total PolitiFact revenues in the previous calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PolitiFact does not accept donations from anonymous sources, political parties, elected officials or candidates seeking public office, or any other source considered a conflict of interest. Disclosed funding aims to maintain reader trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics policy for journalists' public conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact journalists avoid the public expression of political opinion and public involvement in the political process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff do not make political contributions, work on campaigns, sign online petitions, post yard signs or participate in political marches. They avoid expressing political views on social media and avoid snarky commentary. Voting is a private matter; the policy applies to full-time staffers, correspondents and interns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Because we can't feasibly check all claims, we select the most newsworthy and significant ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In deciding which statements to check, consider: Is the statement rooted in a fact that is verifiable? Does the statement seem misleading or sound wrong? Is the statement significant (avoid minor 'gotchas')? Is it likely to be passed on and repeated? Would a typical person hear or read the statement and wonder: Is that true? PolitiFact tries to select facts from both Democrats and Republicans but more often checks the party in power or repeat offenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not check opinions or allowable rhetorical license
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t check opinions, and we recognize that in the world of speechmaking and political rhetoric, there is license for hyperbole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only statements rooted in verifiable facts are appropriate for fact-checking; rhetorical exaggeration and subjective opinion should generally be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-record sourcing and source publication
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact uses on-the-record interviews and publishes a list of sources with every fact-check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, the source list includes links to freely available sources (some may be behind paywalls). The goal is to help readers judge whether they agree with the ruling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always attempt to contact the speaker/source
rubrics_metrics.description: We always contact or attempt to contact the person, website or organization that made the statement we are fact-checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifying the source is a standard part of the reporting process and helps ensure fairness and accuracy; responses received may be included as updates if they don't change conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on primary sources and original documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: We emphasize primary sources and original documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek direct access to government reports, academic studies and other data. It’s not sufficient to get something second-hand. We don’t rely on what a campaign or elected official tells us — we verify it independently. If relying on news reports that use unnamed sources, note inability to independently verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard reporting process for fact-checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Every fact-check generally includes: a review of what other fact-checkers have found; a thorough Google search; a search of online databases; consultation with a variety of experts; a review of publications and a final overall review of available evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This multi-step approach is the baseline investigative method; processes may vary by item, but emphasis is on thoroughness and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth-O-Meter rating scale and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Truth-O-Meter has six ratings, in decreasing level of truthfulness: TRUE; MOSTLY TRUE; HALF TRUE; MOSTLY FALSE; FALSE; PANTS ON FIRE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each rating has a definition: TRUE = statement accurate with nothing significant missing; MOSTLY TRUE = accurate but needs clarification/additional info; HALF TRUE = partially accurate but leaves out important details or takes things out of context; MOSTLY FALSE = contains an element of truth but ignores critical facts that would give a different impression; FALSE = not accurate; PANTS ON FIRE = not accurate and makes a ridiculous claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof and timing for ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of proof is on the speaker, and we rate statements based on the information known at the time the statement is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings reflect evidence available at the time of the claim; new evidence may prompt updates or corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating decision workflow and adjudication questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The reporter suggests a rating; the editor and reporter review together; assigning editor brings the rated fact-check to two additional editors; the three editors and reporter discuss and vote (two votes carry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During review they ask: Is the statement literally true? Is there another way to read it? Did the speaker provide evidence? How have we handled similar statements in the past? What is PolitiFact’s jurisprudence? The group may make edits and changes before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flip-O-Meter ratings and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Flip-O-Meter rates an official's consistency on an issue and has three ratings: NO FLIP; HALF FLIP; FULL FLOP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Flip-O-Meter is not a value judgment about changing positions; it analyzes the shift and degree of change, with a reporting/editing process similar to Truth-O-Meter fact-checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and criteria for tracking campaign promises
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact tracks campaign promises based on verifiable outcomes, not on intentions or effort. A promise is defined as a prospective statement of an action or outcome that is verifiable; all promises list the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promise meters are created by reviewing speeches, TV appearances, position papers and campaign websites. Ratings reflect observable progress or fulfillment rather than motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise-meter rating categories and dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Promise meters have six ratings: NOT YET RATED; IN THE WORKS; STALLED; COMPROMISE; PROMISE KEPT; PROMISE BROKEN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not Yet Rated is the default until evidence appears. IN THE WORKS = proposed/being considered; STALLED = no movement; COMPROMISE = substantially less than original but some accomplishment; PROMISE KEPT = mostly/completely fulfilled; PROMISE BROKEN = not fulfilled. Ratings can change over time as circumstances change (e.g., In the Works → Stalled → In the Works).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and updates policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact corrects errors as quickly as possible and with appropriate transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major errors that change the rating receive a mark of correction at the top, the text is updated, an archived copy preserved and linked, and the item is tagged 'Corrections and updates.' Errors of fact that do not impact the rating receive a correction at the bottom and the tag. Typos and small errors are corrected without a mark. Updates (new non-corrective information) receive an 'Corrections and updates' tag and may be added parenthetically or at the end. Editor’s notes may be used to alert readers to helpful context without changing the original report.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN) commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact is a verified signatory of the IFCN’s code of principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IFCN principles include commitments to nonpartisanship and fairness; transparency of sources, funding and methodology; and open and honest corrections. PolitiFact renews its IFCN commitment annually and links to the application and independent assessment publicly. The IFCN offers a complaint process for alleged significant violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media partnership roles and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact partners with Facebook and TikTok; PolitiFact fact-checkers examine flagged posts and provide feedback to the social media companies as to the accuracy of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While PolitiFact determines the accuracy of the posts, the platforms decide what, if any, action to take on their platforms. Links provided explain partnership details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid trivial 'gotchas' and prioritize significance
rubrics_metrics.description: We avoid minor 'gotchas' on claims that are obviously a slip of the tongue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection prioritizes significance and likely readership impact over petty errors or slips that do not change meaning materially.
